name: Diploma of Nursing
description: This course builds the clinical skills of an enrolled nurse. Students practise in simulation labs on the wards-in-miniature before supervised clinical blocks. Theory covers anatomy, medication safety and care planning across the lifespan.

name: Diploma of Ageing Support and Care
description: Learn how to support older people to stay well and independent at home or in residential care. Classes mix case discussion with hands-on practice in personal care, dementia communication and safe manual handling. Work placements run alongside the study year.

name: Diploma of Population Health Promotion
description: Students look at how communities stay healthy and how programs are planned to help them. Projects ask learners to design a small health campaign, collect simple local data and present it to a group. The course suits people already working in community or youth settings.

name: Diploma of Health Services Administration
description: This course covers the front-of-house and back-office work that keeps a clinic or ward running. Students learn records, scheduling, billing codes and privacy rules through scenario tasks and software practice. A short workplace project closes the year.

name: Diploma of Nutrition and Wellbeing
description: A practical introduction to food, nutrition and healthy habits. Students plan meals for different groups, read food labels and learn to give simple, evidence-based advice. Placements take place in community kitchens and care settings.

name: Diploma of Allied Health Assistance
description: Students train to assist physiotherapists, occupational therapists and other allied health professionals. Study combines exercise programs, mobility aids and rehabilitation basics with supervised practice on real caseloads. Assessment is mostly by practical demonstration.

name: Diploma of Genetic Health Support
description: An entry course for people who want to work in clinics where families learn about inherited conditions. Students study basic genetics, family histories and respectful, clear communication. Teaching is by case studies and role play rather than laboratory work.

name: Master of Nursing Practice
description: For graduates in another field who want to become registered nurses. The program moves from foundational skills in simulation labs to extended clinical placements across medical, surgical and community settings. Assessments include reflective portfolios, case analysis and practical examinations.

name: Master of Public Health
description: Students learn how health problems are measured and addressed across whole populations. The course teaches epidemiology and biostatistics through worked data sets, then applies them in program planning and policy units. A final project examines a real public health question.

name: Master of Health Services Management
description: This one-year course prepares clinicians and administrators to lead teams and services in hospitals, clinics and aged care. Students work on budgets, workforce planning and quality improvement using case material from health organisations. Seminars are run in the evenings.

name: Master of Clinical Exercise Physiology
description: Students learn to design exercise programs for people living with heart disease, diabetes, cancer and other chronic conditions. Time is split between laboratory testing, clinical theory and supervised placements. The course finishes with an applied research project.

name: Diploma of Health Science
description: A bridging diploma that introduces the main ideas behind nursing, allied health and public health. Students study biology, communication and study skills in small tutorial groups. It is designed as a pathway into a degree in health.

name: Master of Health Professional Education
description: For health practitioners who supervise students or train colleagues. The course covers how adults learn, how to design a clinical teaching session and how to give fair feedback. Students trial their own teaching plans in their workplaces.

name: Master of Nutrition and Dietetics
description: This course prepares students to become dietitians. They study food science, medical nutrition therapy and community nutrition, and practise counselling in role-played consultations. Several placement blocks across hospital, community and food service settings are built into the second year.

name: Master of Public Health (Health Promotion)
description: Aimed at people who want to plan programs that keep communities well. The course teaches how to assess needs, design interventions and judge whether they worked. Students complete a project with a community partner in the final semester.

name: Master of Physiotherapy Studies
description: Graduates of a related science degree train as physiotherapists. Teaching centres on movement analysis, musculoskeletal and neurological rehabilitation, and clinical reasoning, with workshops in practical skills each week. Students take extended placements in hospitals and community clinics.

name: Master of Health Administration
description: A one-year course in running health organisations. Units cover governance, health economics, information systems and managing people in clinical environments. Students work through case studies from public and private services.

name: Diploma of Community Health and Ageing
description: A first-year course in supporting older adults in community settings. It looks at healthy ageing, chronic illness and the services available to families. Students visit local programs and complete a placement with an aged care provider.

name: Master of Mental Health Nursing
description: For registered nurses moving into mental health. The program covers assessment, therapeutic communication, medication and recovery-oriented care, and uses simulation to practise difficult conversations. Clinical blocks are held in inpatient and community mental health teams.

name: Master of Nursing (Nurse Practitioner)
description: An advanced course for experienced registered nurses who want to work with a wider scope, diagnosing and prescribing under guidelines. Teaching combines advanced assessment, pharmacology and clinical reasoning with mentored practice in the student's own specialty. Case presentations form much of the assessment.

name: Master of Public Health
description: Students examine health across populations, from infectious disease to chronic conditions. Units move from core epidemiology and statistics to policy analysis and community program design. A capstone allows learners to work on a question linked to their own interests.

name: Master of Genetic Counselling
description: This course trains students to help people understand inherited conditions and make informed decisions about testing. Learning combines human genetics, counselling theory and practice interviews with actors, followed by supervised clinical placements. Students also study ethics, consent and how to explain risk clearly.

name: Master of Health Services Management
description: This course develops managers for hospitals, community services and aged care providers. Students analyse budgets, service models and quality systems and lead a change project in their own workplace. Delivery is in short intensive blocks.

name: Diploma of Health and Nutrition Studies
description: A short introduction to health science with a focus on food and lifestyle. Students learn the basics of physiology, nutrition and how to read research. Tutorials stress clear writing and practical problem solving, preparing students for further study.

name: Master of Midwifery
description: For registered nurses who want to become midwives. The course teaches normal pregnancy, birth and newborn care and when to refer for obstetric help. Students follow women through their pregnancies as part of continuity-of-care placements.

name: Master of Public Health
description: The course builds skills in measuring health problems and designing responses at community and state level. Students use real data sets in statistics classes and prepare policy briefs for assessment. Electives let them lean towards mental health, environment or global settings.

name: Master of Health Data Analytics
description: Students learn how health records, hospital data and survey results are cleaned, analysed and reported. The course uses statistical software and small projects built on de-identified data. It suits graduates who want to work with information rather than patients.
units: Privacy and Ethics in Health Data

name: Master of Genetic Counselling and Genomics
description: Combines laboratory-based genetics with the communication skills needed in a counselling clinic. Students interpret test results, practise telling families what they mean and learn how to support decisions without steering them. Placements in genetics clinics take up much of the second year.

name: Diploma of Health Care Management
description: Designed for team leaders in clinics and care services. Students learn to roster staff, manage small budgets and handle difficult conversations. Assessments are workplace tasks, written from the student's own experience.

name: Master of Occupational Therapy Studies
description: Graduates of other degrees train to help people take part in daily life after injury, illness or disability. Practical classes cover assessment, adaptive equipment and therapeutic activities, and students apply them in several placement blocks. Study also includes research and professional reasoning.

name: Master of Health Psychology and Wellbeing
description: Looks at how habits, stress and illness affect each other. Students study behaviour change models, chronic illness adjustment and workplace wellbeing programs. Learning is by seminar and a supervised project in a health setting.

name: Master of Nursing Practice
description: Aimed at graduates who want to become registered nurses. Students build clinical skills in simulation before long placements in hospital wards and rural community services. The course highlights care for small and remote communities.

name: Master of Public Health (Rural and Remote)
description: This course studies how health is protected and promoted outside the big cities. Students learn epidemiology and planning with examples from island and rural communities. A research project is carried out with a regional service.

name: Master of Genetic Counselling Practice
description: Students learn to guide patients and families through genetic testing and results. Studies cover inheritance, common conditions, counselling skills and the legal side of using genetic information. Case discussions and practice sessions feed into supervised placements.

name: Diploma of Health and Community Studies
description: A foundation year for students interested in community health, nursing or social care. It introduces human biology, the Australian health system and how to study at university level. Small class sizes give plenty of room for questions.

name: Master of Dementia Care
description: A course for practitioners who care for people with dementia and their families. It covers the biology of dementia, communication approaches, behaviour support and care planning. Much of the teaching is online, with a workplace project at the end.

name: Master of Health Services Management
description: This course covers management in public and private health services. Students study planning, finance and clinical governance, with attention to services delivered over long distances. Online units are combined with a short residential school.

name: Master of Public Health
description: Students learn to find out what makes communities unwell and to design practical responses. The course covers epidemiology, health policy and program evaluation, and each study period includes group work on realistic scenarios. A final project takes a topic from idea to written report.

name: Master of Clinical Rehabilitation
description: This course prepares students for rehabilitation work with people recovering from injury and long-term illness. Teaching covers assessment, goal setting and return-to-work planning, supported by clinic-based placements. Students also study pain, disability and the insurance systems around them.

name: Master of Nutrition and Food Science
description: A one-year course linking what is in food to how it affects health. Students use laboratory sessions to analyse foods and seminars to study nutrition research. It suits scientists who want to move into food policy or product development.

name: Diploma of Nursing Studies
description: A two-year entry course to nursing. Students learn core clinical skills in practice labs and then apply them in supervised placements. Subjects include anatomy, medication safety and communicating with patients and families.

name: Master of Genetic Counselling Studies
description: Students prepare to work with families who are facing decisions about inherited disease. The course combines genetics, psychology and ethics, with simulated counselling sessions each week. Placements in clinical genetics services build practical experience.

name: Master of Ageing and Community Care
description: Looks at how services can help people age well in their own communities. Students study home care models, carer support and policy, and develop a service improvement proposal for assessment. Teaching is mostly by discussion of case examples.

name: Master of Public Health and Epidemiology
description: This course emphasises the numbers behind public health decisions. Students learn to design studies, analyse data and report findings, using statistical software throughout. Elective units allow a focus on infectious disease, chronic disease or health inequality.

name: Master of Genetic Counselling
description: Students learn how to explain genetic conditions, discuss testing options and support people through hard news. Study blends genetics and genomics with counselling skills practised in role plays and observed sessions. Clinical placements are completed across genetic and specialist services.

name: Master of Nursing Practice
description: A pathway for graduates of other fields into registered nursing. Students develop clinical judgment in simulation, then practise in acute, community and mental health settings. Assessments include case studies, practical skills checks and reflective writing.

name: Master of Health Services Management
description: For people working in or moving towards management of hospitals, clinics and community services. Units cover policy, finance, quality improvement and people management, taught by seminar and workplace project. The year closes with a service redesign proposal.

name: Diploma of Health Sciences
description: A foundation year for students aiming at nursing, physiotherapy and public health degrees. Classes introduce biology, chemistry and statistics at an approachable pace. Tutors stress reading, writing and exam skills.

name: Master of Physiotherapy
description: A professional course that prepares graduates of related science degrees for practice. Students study movement, pain and rehabilitation, and apply their learning in labs and clinical placements across hospital and community settings. Research skills are taught alongside practice.

name: Master of Public Health
description: Students learn to plan and judge programs that protect and improve community health. Units build epidemiology, statistics and health policy knowledge, and group projects use data from regional communities. A capstone brings the strands together.

name: Master of Nutrition and Dietetics
description: This is a professional course for those who want to work as dietitians. It teaches the science of nutrition, how to adjust diets for illness and how to counsel people with different needs. Placements in hospitals, community services and food service units are spread through the second year.

name: Master of Nursing Practice
description: Graduates of another degree retrain as registered nurses. Clinical skills are taught in practice labs and then used on placements in regional hospitals and community clinics. Teaching also looks at caring for people in smaller towns.

name: Diploma of Health and Wellbeing
description: A year of study that introduces health science and ways to support wellbeing in everyday settings. Students learn about exercise, nutrition and mental health, and practise simple coaching skills. The course serves as a stepping stone to further study.

name: Master of Health Promotion and Ageing
description: Focuses on keeping older adults active, connected and well. Students review evidence on falls, loneliness and chronic illness, then design a small community project. Study is largely online with workshops on campus.

name: Master of Health Informatics
description: This course teaches how electronic health records and clinical information systems are built and used. Students handle de-identified data, learn standards for sharing records and work in teams on a systems project. Privacy and safe use of data are central themes.
